newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Acacia criticises Reserve Bank gold sales.
newsitem.headline: Acacia criticises Reserve Bank gold sales.

text.p: Gold producer Acacia Resources Ltd on Friday criticised the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) decision to sell down 167 tonnes of gold reserves.

"If the Reserve Bank...say they have no confidence they are going to get any return out of holding gold, what does that mean for Australia's second largest export industry?" said Acacia managing director Michael Folie.
"It's more than disappointing...it really does impact on confidence around the world," Folie told Reuters.
Gold prices slumped to a 12-year low in offshore markets on Thursday on news the RBA had sold the gold in recent months.
Folie said he believed gold still had a role to play in the inernational reserve system as it provided a spread on assets and avoided exchange rate risk.
While the bank said Australia had reserves in the ground, capital and labour still needed to be invested to recover the gold, he said.
The sell-down and resulting blow to confidence in the sector would also make it harder to attract offshore capital and help the industry expand.
Folie said a low gold price would lead to a shake-out in the industry, which was a large employer and investor in regional Australia, with high-cost producers likely to close.
Australian gold exports generated revenue of A$5.7 billion in 1995/96, making it the second largest export industry, excluding tourism, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics.
Coal exports generated revenue of A$7.8 million.
Acacia was trading down three cents at A$1.65 at 12.10 p.m. (0210 GMT).
